text:
[LSTR.1.1] A `String` value is a sequence of Unicode codepoints.
Every codepoint in `[U+0001, U+10FFFF]` is admissible except the
surrogate range `[U+D800, U+DFFF]`, which is forbidden per RFC
3629. **U+0000 is not admissible:** no `String` holds it. A literal that
would spell it is a compile error ([LGRA.2.9.4]), and a value that would carry
it is refused where it enters ([LSTR.1.5]).

idris.name: Lstr_1_1__text
idris.note: A String value's text: a sequence of Unicode codepoints, each a natural. Admissibility is not carried as an index: the fixture runner refuses a `string` record carrying a codepoint `lstr_1_1__admissible` rejects where it enters, so every text the model is run on is admissible, and the model's functions are total on every list of naturals.

idris.name: lstr_1_1__admissible
idris.note: The clause's range: U+0001 to U+10FFFF less the surrogates U+D800 to U+DFFF, and never U+0000.

idris.name: lstr_1_1__text_admissible
idris.note: Every codepoint of a text admissible: what the fixture runner decides of a `string` record. The compile error on a literal and the refusal where a value enters are the compiler's and the runtime's, outside the model.
